### Subject: Opinion on taxability of transfer of the Consumer Electronics Division as a slump sale under Section 50B

---

## 1. Purpose and Basis of this Opinion

This opinion is issued pursuant to our engagement letter dated [●], and is based solely on the facts and representations furnished by the management of Kavach Industries Limited, and on the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable rules, notifications, circulars, and judicial precedents as they stand on the date hereof. This opinion is addressed solely to, and for the sole use of, Kavach Industries Limited for the specific purpose stated herein, and should not be relied upon, quoted, or disclosed to any third party without our prior written consent.

## 2. Statement of Facts

Kavach Industries Limited transfers its Consumer Electronics Division, comprising all assets, liabilities, and employees, as a going concern to Meridian Holdings Private Limited for a lump-sum consideration of INR 185 crore under a Business Transfer Agreement, with no itemised values assigned to individual assets or liabilities.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether the transfer of the Consumer Electronics Division qualifies as a 'slump sale' under Section 2(42C) and is taxable under Section 50B, and how the resultant capital gains should be computed.

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 2(42C)
- Section 2(19AA)
- Section 50B
- Rule 6H


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- CIT v. Artex Manufacturing Co., (1997) 227 ITR 260 (SC)
- PNB Finance Ltd v. CIT, (2008) 307 ITR 75 (SC)

## 6. Analysis

Since the Business Transfer Agreement conveys the division as a going concern for a lump-sum consideration without assigning values to individual assets or liabilities, the transaction meets the statutory definition of a slump sale as clarified in Artex Manufacturing and PNB Finance. The division has been held for more than 36 months, and gains are accordingly computed as the lump-sum consideration less the 'net worth' of the undertaking, determined per Rule 6H.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

The transaction is a slump sale taxable under Section 50B as long-term capital gains, computed as the sale consideration of INR 185 crore less the net worth of the Consumer Electronics Division as on the date of transfer.

**Confidence level:** High degree of comfort on characterisation; net-worth computation may attract scrutiny
